'''''Salvia pratensis''''', the '''meadow clary'''<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |access-date=17 October 2014 }}</ref> or '''meadow sage''', is  a [[species]] of [[flowering plant]] in the family [[Lamiaceae]], [[native plant|native]] to Europe, western Asia and northern Africa. The Latin [[Binomial nomenclature|specific epithet]] ''pratensis'' means "of [[meadows]]", referring to its preferred habitat. It also grows in scrub edges and woodland borders.

==Description==
This [[herbaceous plant|herbaceous]] [[perennial plant|perennial]] forms a basal clump {{convert|1|to|1.5|m|ft|abbr=on}} tall, with rich green rugose leaves that are slightly ruffled and toothed on the edges. The stems have four edges and are clad in glandular and soft hairs. The leaves are arranged in opposite pairs, with those on the lower part of the stem up to {{convert|15|cm|in|0|abbr=on}} long, decreasing in size higher up the stem. The flower stalks are typically branched, with four to six flowers in each [[whorl (botany)|verticil]] forming a lax spike. The flowers may grow up to {{convert|2.5|cm|in|0|abbr=on}} and open starting from the base of the [[inflorescence]], which grows up to {{convert|30.5|cm|in|0|abbr=on}} long. The small [[sepal|calyx]] is dark brown. The corolla is irregular, {{convert|20|to|30|mm|1|abbr=on}} long, fused with two lips and long-tubed. The upper lip arches in a crescent shape and the lower lip is three-lobed with the central lobe larger than the lateral lobes. In the wild the corolla is usually bluish-violet. In cultivation, the flowers have a wide variety of colors, from rich violet and violet-blue to bluish white, and from pink to pure white. There are two long stamens protected by the upper corolla lip and the fruit is a four-chambered [[schizocarp]].<ref name="Clebsch">{{cite book |last1=Clebsch|first1=Betsy|last2=Barner|first2=Carol D.|title=The New Book of Salvias|publisher=Timber Press|year=2003|page=226|isbn=978-0-88192-560-9|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=NM0iwB8GrQYC&pg=PA226}}</ref><ref name=NatureGate>{{cite web |url=http://www.luontoportti.com/suomi/en/kukkakasvit/meadow-sage |title=Meadow sage: ''Salvia pratensis'' |publisher=NatureGate |access-date=14 December 2013}}</ref>

==Distribution and habitat==
''Salvia pratensis'' is native to Europe, western Asia and northern Africa where it grows in meadows, fields, banks and rough places.<ref name=NatureGate/> It has become naturalized in many parts of the United States, and is considered a noxious weed in the state of Washington.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://plants.usda.gov/java/profile?symbol=SAPR2|title=PLANTS Profile for Salvia pretenses|work=Plants Profile|publisher=United States Department of Agriculture|access-date=26 July 2011}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nwcb.wa.gov/weed_info/Salvia_pratensis.html|title=Meadow Clary|publisher=State of Washington|access-date=26 July 2011|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110927090718/http://www.nwcb.wa.gov/weed_info/Salvia_pratensis.html|archive-date=27 September 2011}}</ref> At one time it was banned from California because it was thought to have naturalized in three locations.

==Cultivation==
''Salvia pratensis'' is hardy in the severest European climates, down to {{convert|-40|C|F|abbr=on}}.<ref>{{cite web |title=Salvia pratensis |url=https://www.darwinperennials.com/Products/Plantinfo/?phid=055007757037241 |website=DarwinPerennials |access-date=3 November 2023}}</ref> It is widely grown in horticulture, especially ''Salvia pratensis'' subsp. ''haematodes'',<ref name="Mark Griffiths 1995">Mark Griffiths, Editor. ''Index of Garden Plants'', 2nd American Edition. (Portland, Oregon: Timber Press, 1995. {{ISBN|0-88192-246-3}}.)</ref> which is prized by flower arrangers as a cut flower. Some botanists consider it a separate species, ''S. haematodes''.<ref name="Clebsch"/>

Named cultivars include:-
* 'Atroviolacea', dark blue to violet
* 'Baumgartenii', blue to violet
* 'Lupinoides', to {{convert|60|cm|in|abbr=on}}, white-flecked blue to purple
* 'Mitsommer' ("Midsummer"), sky blue
* 'Rosea', rose-pink to purple
* 'Rubicunda', rose-red
* 'Tenorii', to about {{convert|60|cm|in|abbr=on}} tall, blue flowers
* 'Variegata', blue and sometimes white-tipped flowers.<ref name="Mark Griffiths 1995"/>

===AGM cultivars===
The cultivar group Haematodes,<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/100935/Salvia-pratensis-Haematodes-Group/Details | title = ''Salvia pratensis'' Haematodes Group | publisher = RHS | access-date = 5 March 2021}}</ref> and the cultivar 'Indigo' with violet blue flowers, have both gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].<ref>{{cite web|title=RHS Plant Selector - ''Salvia pratensis'' 'Indigo'|url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/119289/Salvia-pratensis-Indigo/Details | access-date = 5 March 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/pdfs/agm-lists/agm-ornamentals.pdf | title = AGM Plants - Ornamental 
| date = July 2017 | page = 95 | publisher = Royal Horticultural Society | access-date = 14 October 2018}}</ref>

==Uses==
The name of the plant 'clary' is derived from 'clear-eye' and the plant seeds were historically ground to a paste and used to clear irritations in the eye. It was also used for [[gargle|gargling]] and as an early form of toothpaste, as well as a flavouring for alcohol.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.naturescape.co.uk/product/meadow-clary/#:~:text=Meadow%20Clary%20is%20also%20known,to%20reduce%20inflammation%20or%20redness.|title=Meadow clary |publisher=Natureescape.co.uk |date= |access-date=3 February 2024}}</ref>
